alex: Quick shout: ran into a subtle UX problem in the Go SDK generator when cancelling contexts during an auth token refresh. Repro is tiny and inlines the fake creds below.

alex: ```go
// repro: cancel during slow token refresh
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
creds := &fakeCreds{sleep: 2 * time.Second}
client := NewClient(WithCredentials(creds))

g, _ := client.Generator(ctx, "gpt-lite")
// cancel soon after starting stream
go func() { time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
if _, err := g.Stream(ctx); err != nil { log.Printf("stream err: %v", err) }
// observed: goroutine stuck in creds.Refresh, stream never returns promptly
```

tara: Thanks Alex. Is the blocked goroutine coming from our handshake path or inside the auth library?

alex: Handshake path. The credentials implementation currently blocks and has no ctx param so refresh can't be interrupted. When cancel races with refresh the generator never sees ctx.Done().

ben: Two angles: short-term add a handshake timeout in the client config (e.g. 5s) and update onboarding sample-app; long-term update creds API to `GetToken(ctx)` and make handshake select on ctx earlier.

nina: For DX parity with other SDKs, prefer making creds context-aware. Also add generator.Close()/Abort() as a backwards-compatible escape hatch.

ci-bot: [ci] Detected increase in goroutines for generator e2e on canary. Ticket INF-3337 opened.

alex: Plan: 1) add handshake timeout default, 2) update sample app showing `context.WithTimeout` + pattern to call `g.Abort()`, 3) follow-up PR to change creds interface to accept context and add migration shim. I'll open an RFC/PR draft.

tara: Please add a unit test that simulates slow creds and asserts no goroutine leaks post-cancel. Also add a short blurb in the Go SDK README under "Cancellation & Timeouts".

ben: I'll sketch the migration snippet for CHANGELOG showing how to implement the shim for older creds implementations.

alex: Great. Putting this in the SDK parity triage list. Posting repro in the issue so folks can run locally.
